docs: # Instructions
Nine implemented instructions: initialize, record_contribution,
burn_claims, prepay_renter, refund_renter, pause, resume, and two
authority rotations — plus six M11 settlement handlers that are
DECLARED with `todo!()` bodies (M11-A stubs, at the bottom of this
module). There is intentionally no `transfer_claim`, no `close_claim`,
no instruction that takes depositor USDC as principal — the absence of
an instruction IS a security property here (rules 1, 9 and 10).

instructions.name: burn_claims
docs: Exit a depositor's record: burn `amount` claims from their claim
account. NO USDC moves (D40) — principal was never on-chain money;
depositor-bound USDC only ever flows OUT via M11 settle payouts,
which reuse this instruction's account shapes.
Signers — THE TWO DOORS: `backend_authority` (assisted; the
operator submitting for a custodial depositor, rule 10) OR the
depositor's own key (direct; the escape hatch that keeps exit
possible when the operator is evil or offline). With neither
signature the instruction refuses. The M11 exit ceiling attaches
identically on both doors, inside `check_withdrawal_ceiling`.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The one signer — WHICH door it opens is decided in the handler:
backend_authority (assisted) or `depositor` (direct). No `mut`:
burning pays no rent and moves no lamports.

accounts.name: claim_account
docs: The `depositor` argument is bound to the seeds here — anchor
verifies this account IS `[claim, <that pubkey>]`, so the burned
balance is provably the named depositor's registry row.

instructions.name: challenge
docs: Challenge a root: freeze its payouts. Permissionless — any key may
challenge, inside the window (SPEC §10).
Doctrine: invariant 5 — `clock.slot` must be inside
`posted_at + CHALLENGE_WINDOW_SLOTS`, or the challenge refuses with
`ChallengeWindowClosed`; the root turns `Challenged`, its claims
freeze until the multisig rules, and `stands_ruled` is cleared (a new
challenge outranks an earlier "stands"). Emits `RootChallenged`.

accounts.name: challenger
docs: Any funded key.

accounts.name: settlement_root
docs: `has_one = pool`: a root can only be challenged through ITS pool.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Claim one leaf: verify the inclusion proof against the published
root, pay `amount` USDC from the vault to the leaf's named
`depositor`, write the leaf's claim marker, and add `amount` to the
root's `paid_out`.
Doctrine: invariant 2 — a proof that does not hash up to the root
refuses with `InvalidProof`; invariant 3 — the marker is plain
`init`, so a replayed leaf dies at account creation, and the proof
is bound to its index; invariant 4 — THE TWO DOORS (the backend, or
`depositor`'s own key — anything else is `ExitAuthority`) and the
destination must be owned by `depositor`; invariant 5 — a root that
is not `Active` refuses with `RootFrozen`; invariant 11 — a root
whose challenge window is still open refuses with
`ChallengeWindowOpen`, unless the multisig ruled it stands; invariant
12 — a claim that would push `paid_out` past `total_payout` refuses
with `PayoutExceedsTotal`. Emits `ClaimPaid`.
Session B owes the FIRST TWO of these IN THIS ORDER — the suite pins
which refusal a shape gets: (1) the status, else `RootFrozen`;
(2) the window, else `ChallengeWindowOpen`. A root challenged while
still INSIDE its window is frozen, not merely delayed. After those:
the proof, the door, the declared total, then the transfer, the
marker and `paid_out += amount`.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The one signer — WHICH door it opens is decided in the handler.

accounts.name: settlement_root
docs: The root the proof must verify against. `mut`: the handler counts the
payout on it (`paid_out`, invariant 12) — without `mut` Anchor never
serializes the update back, so the write is silently dropped.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Where the payout lands. `owner == depositor` is an ACCOUNT
CONSTRAINT: neither door can route a payout anywhere else
(invariant 4).

accounts.name: vault
docs: Escrow source — pool-owned; only this instruction can draw on it.

accounts.name: claim_marker
docs: Plain `init`: the marker can be born ONCE per leaf. A replay fails
HERE, in account creation, before any handler logic runs
(invariant 3).

accounts.name: payer
docs: Rent payer for the marker. A SEPARATE account from `authority` so the
direct door needs nothing from the depositor but their signature: any
funded key (the transaction's fee payer, a relayer) can pay.

accounts.name: clock
docs: The clock, DECLARED like in `post_root` and `challenge`: the handler
reads the slot from it to apply the challenge-window rule
(invariant 11).

accounts.name: token_program
docs: Token v3 ONLY. No Token-2022 program and no mint account appear in
this list: a claim moves USDC and cannot mint anything
(invariant 9).

instructions.name: fund_bond
docs: Bond the operator: move `amount` USDC from the operator's OWN wallet
into the bond vault and grow the bond record. Backend-signed (the
operator bonds its own money); emits `BondFunded`.
Session B owes: the transfer, the record increment, the event, and
the usual refusals (paused pool, zero amount).

accounts.name: backend_authority
docs: The operator's hot key — gate AND rent payer.

accounts.name: source
docs: Where the bond comes from: a wallet the BACKEND owns, on the pool's
USDC mint (the operator bonds its own money).

accounts.name: usdc_mint
docs: The pool's USDC mint, as a typed ACCOUNT: Anchor's token-account
init can only bind `token::mint` to an account field, so the mint
rides along here and is pinned to the pool's own below (a foreign
mint cannot give birth to the bond vault).

accounts.name: bond_vault
docs: The bond vault: a pool-owned token account, so no key can move the
bond directly — only `slash_bond` (a satisfied instruction) can.

accounts.name: bond
docs: The bond record. `init_if_needed`: first funding creates it, later
fundings top it up (every reuse re-verifies seeds and owner).

instructions.name: initialize
docs: One-time pool bootstrap. Creates the config PDA, the Token-2022
`NonTransferable` claim mint, and the USDC vault. Called by the
deployer immediately after program deploy; the `admin_authority`
passed in is the Squads multisig vault PDA (computed before this
call from the multisig's create key).
# Who may call it — the A-041 gate (deployment front-run)
The FIRST caller no longer wins: this instruction requires the
signature of THIS DEPLOYMENT'S UPGRADE AUTHORITY — the key or PDA
the BPF loader recorded in the program's ProgramData account when
the program was deployed. On devnet that authority is the Squads
multisig vault (2-of-2), so the pool cannot come into existence
without a 2-of-2 vote executing this instruction — the vault PDA's
signature arrives exactly the way `AdminGate`'s `admin_authority`
signatures do (Squads `execute_transaction` produces them
cross-program). Between deploy and initialize the singleton cannot
be captured: an attacker landing there has no multisig signature,
their initialize refuses (atomically — nothing is created), and
the operator's identical call succeeds whenever it lands. The dev
deploy key pays rent and holds nothing. An immutable deployment
(ProgramData authority `None`) can never birth a pool — refused
with the same error.

accounts.name: pool
docs: The singleton config PDA — `init` makes this instruction once-only
(a second call finds the account occupied and aborts).

accounts.name: claim_mint
docs: The claim registry mint PDA — initialized MANUALLY in the handler
(anchor-spl 1.x has no non_transferable account constraint): the
Token-2022 NonTransferable extension is initialized before any
supply exists, making transfers of this mint reject at the TOKEN
PROGRAM level forever (rule 9 enforcement at the lowest layer).
Mint authority is the pool PDA — only `record_contribution`
mints, only `burn_claims` burns.
CREATED and initialized by the handler's CPIs in this same
transaction (allocate -> NonTransferable -> mint state), so before
the handler runs it is an empty system account. The seeds
constraint above is the address check; the CPI chain is the
ownership check (it can only land on the Token-2022 program).

accounts.name: usdc_mint
docs: Existing USDC mint (SPL Token v3 on devnet — Circle faucet USDC).
The decimals constraint pins the micro-USD seam at bootstrap: a
non-6-decimals "USDC" cannot be custodied by this pool.

accounts.name: vault
docs: The escrow vault: a PDA token account, owner = pool PDA, so ONLY
this program (deposit/withdraw handlers) can ever move custodial
USDC. No human key, including the multisig's, signs token moves.

accounts.name: authority
docs: Deployer (payer for the PDAs and rent). On devnet this is the
session deploy key; it receives NO standing authority — the admin
and backend authorities arrive as instruction arguments.

accounts.name: program_data
docs: The BPF loader's ProgramData account FOR THIS PROGRAM — the
deployment-authority source the A-041 gate reads (see handler).
Checked accounts: exact loader-derived address + loader owner +
ProgramData variant, all verified there. Read-only.
loader-derived ProgramData PDA of `crate::ID`, owner = the BPF
Upgradeable Loader, bytes = ProgramData variant with a Some
authority); the required signature is enforced on
`upgrade_authority` below. UncheckedAccount (not AccountInfo)
because anchor's derive must add nothing here — the handler IS
the check.

accounts.name: upgrade_authority
docs: THIS deployment's upgrade authority (devnet: the Squads multisig
vault PDA, signing via a 2-of-2 `execute_transaction`). The
`Signer` type makes the runtime verify the signature; the handler
additionally requires the key to equal the ProgramData-declared
authority. This is the A-041 gate: without it, initialize is
refused and the singleton stays unborn.

accounts.name: rent
docs: The rent sysvar, DECLARED even though on-chain code could fetch it
via syscall: host-side test execution (program-test builtins) has no
syscalls — sysvars arrive only as accounts — so declaring it keeps
the program runnable in both worlds. Read-only, one account in the
list, zero lamports.

instructions.name: pause
docs: Admin circuit breaker — halt deposits and withdrawals. Signed by
`admin_authority` only (the multisig vault PDA on devnet).

accounts.name: admin_authority
docs: The multisig vault PDA (devnet). A Signer constraint — the runtime
verifies PDA signatures cross-program, so this accepts either a
plain key (tests) or the Squads-executed vault signature (devnet).

instructions.name: post_root
docs: Post a settlement root: record, for `window`, the Merkle root and
the total it pays, backed by the operator's current bond and stamped
with the slot (the challenge window starts here).
Doctrine: invariant 1 — `total_payout > vault.amount` refuses with
`RootExceedsVault` and NOTHING is created or moved; invariant 7 — a
second root for the same window dies at account creation (the
`SettlementRoot` PDA is plain `init`), so roots are append-only.
A fresh root starts `Active` with `stands_ruled = false` and
`paid_out = 0` (invariants 11 and 12 read both). Emits `RootPosted`.

accounts.name: backend_authority
docs: The operator posts roots: a root is the operator's ATTESTATION of
what the books say the window owes (A-039's caveat, by design).

accounts.name: settlement_root
docs: Plain `init`: the account can be born ONCE per window. A second root
for the same window fails HERE, in account creation (invariant 7).

accounts.name: vault
docs: The escrow the root will be paid from — read for the ceiling check.

accounts.name: bond
docs: The bond backing the root. Not `init`: a root cannot be posted
without an existing bond (SPEC §10 — BONDED operators).

accounts.name: clock
docs: The clock, DECLARED like the rent sysvar in `initialize`: the suite
passes it as an account so host and SBF execution read the same
source of slots.

instructions.name: prepay_renter
docs: Renter prepayment: move `amount` USDC from the renter's token
account into the vault, and increment the renter's OWN prepaid
record `[prepaid, renter]`. This is the ONLY way USDC enters the
protocol (D40) — the M10 rail: metering, checkout and pro-rata
consumption live OFF-chain (M9/M10); this pair is what they plug
into.
Signers: `backend_authority` (operator gate — uninvited money must
not create uninvited liabilities) AND `renter_key` (the source
account's owner: the renter's custodial key on devnet, or the
renter themselves in self-custody). Prepay has no direct-door
variant by design: money IN always needs the source owner's
signature anyway — the token program enforces it.

accounts.name: backend_authority
docs: Operator gate signer; also pays the prepaid record's rent on
first prepay (renters never pay chain costs).

accounts.name: renter_key
docs: The renter identity key — owner of `source`. Custodial on devnet
(the backend holds it) or self-custody in the direct future; the
token program only cares that it owns the source account.

accounts.name: source
docs: Where the prepayment comes from: must be owned by `renter_key` on
the pool's USDC mint.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Escrow destination (seeds re-checked against the config).

accounts.name: prepaid
docs: The renter's OWN prepaid record: `[prepaid, renter]`, owned by the
program. `init_if_needed`: first prepay lazily creates it; refunds
are bounded by this record's `amount` — an on-chain fact.

instructions.name: record_contribution
docs: Record a depositor contribution: mint `amount` claims into the
depositor's program-owned claim account. NO USDC moves (D40) —
principal is Path-B credits on the operator's books (rule 1); the
claim records the micro-USD valuation of what the books say the
depositor contributed.
Signer: `backend_authority` ONLY — this is an operator ATTESTATION
from the books, not a user action. (A self-service mint would let
anyone claim arbitrary contributions; the depositor's power is the
OTHER door — `burn_claims`.) The known limitation: on-chain code
cannot see the books, so a rogue backend could attest fake
contributions — containment is the M11 challenge window + multisig
pause/rotate (AUDIT A-039).

accounts.name: pool
docs: `has_one` checks `pool.backend_authority == backend_authority.key()`
— recording is an operator ATTESTATION from the books, so the
backend gate is the whole signer story (see handler docs: the
depositor's power is the OTHER door, `burn_claims`).

accounts.name: backend_authority
docs: Operator backend hot key; also pays the claim account's rent on
first record (depositors never pay anything).

accounts.name: claim_mint
docs: The registry mint (seeds re-checked; typed so decimals/authority
are constraint-verified on every record).

accounts.name: claim_account
docs: The depositor's registry row: `[claim, depositor]`, owned by the
POOL (not the depositor) — no holder key can burn or close it.
`init_if_needed`: first record lazily creates the row; later
records reuse it (the program pays rent via backend_authority).

instructions.name: refund_renter
docs: Renter refund: move `amount` USDC from the vault to the renter's
destination account, bounded by the renter's OWN on-chain prepaid
record (`amount ≤ prepaid.amount`), and decrement that record.
With the vault holding only renter money (D40), this is the
depositor-independent refund rail M10 composes with — separability
is an on-chain fact here, not a promise.
Signers — THE TWO DOORS (same policy as `burn_claims`):
`backend_authority` (assisted) OR the renter's own key (direct
exit without operator cooperation). Destination routing is pinned
to the renter on both doors, so the backend can never route a
refund to itself.

accounts.name: authority
docs: The one signer — WHICH door it opens is decided in the handler.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Refund destination must belong to the renter being refunded.

accounts.name: vault
docs: Escrow source (seeds re-checked; pool-owned, so only this
program's refund/settle logic can ever move it).

accounts.name: prepaid
docs: The renter's prepaid record — the refund ceiling. Its seeds bind
the `renter` argument, so one renter can never spend another's
record.

instructions.name: resolve_challenge
docs: The multisig rules on a challenge. `Ruling::RootStands` returns the
root to `Active` and sets `stands_ruled` — the ruling waives the rest
of the challenge window (invariant 11); `Ruling::RootFalse {
slash_amount, victim }` marks it `ProvenFalse` and records the exact
slash and the victim.
Doctrine: invariant 6 — a ruling may not exceed the bond that backs
the root (`SlashExceedsBond`); a ruling that the root stands
slashes nothing, ever. Emits `ChallengeResolved`.

accounts.name: admin_authority
docs: The multisig vault PDA on devnet (a plain key in tests).

accounts.name: bond
docs: Read here so the handler can refuse a ruling larger than the bond.

instructions.name: resume
docs: Admin circuit breaker release.

accounts.name: admin_authority
docs: The multisig vault PDA (devnet). A Signer constraint — the runtime
verifies PDA signatures cross-program, so this accepts either a
plain key (tests) or the Squads-executed vault signature (devnet).

instructions.name: set_admin_authority
docs: Rotate the admin authority itself (multisig migration). Admin-only:
changing the admin requires the CURRENT admin's signature — on
devnet that means a 2-of-2 vote.

accounts.name: admin_authority
docs: The multisig vault PDA (devnet). A Signer constraint — the runtime
verifies PDA signatures cross-program, so this accepts either a
plain key (tests) or the Squads-executed vault signature (devnet).

instructions.name: set_backend_authority
docs: Rotate the operator backend hot key (compromise response,
key rollover). Admin-only — the backend cannot re-key itself.

accounts.name: admin_authority
docs: The multisig vault PDA (devnet). A Signer constraint — the runtime
verifies PDA signatures cross-program, so this accepts either a
plain key (tests) or the Squads-executed vault signature (devnet).

instructions.name: slash_bond
docs: Execute a ruled slash: move EXACTLY the recorded `ruled_slash` from
the bond vault to the recorded victim. Permissionless to crank — the
ruling was the multisig's act, and the amount and the destination
come from the root account, never from arguments.
Doctrine: invariant 6 — anything but a `ProvenFalse` root refuses
with `RootNotProvenFalse` (never challenged, still challenged, ruled
to stand, or already slashed); a second slash is therefore
impossible.
Session B owes these checks IN THIS ORDER, because the suite pins
which refusal a shape gets: (1) `RootNotProvenFalse` unless the
root is `ProvenFalse`; (2) `WrongDestinationOwner` unless
`destination.owner == settlement_root.victim` (a handler check, not
an account constraint — see `SlashBond`); (3) move EXACTLY
`ruled_slash`, mark the root `Slashed`, emit `BondSlashed`.

accounts.name: destination
docs: Where the slash lands. The OWNER check lives in the handler, AFTER
the status check — on purpose: as an account constraint it would
fire first for every root with no victim on record, and a slash of
an un-ruled root would be reported as a destination error instead
of `RootNotProvenFalse`. Only the mint check stays here (nothing but
the pool's USDC is ever a payout leg).

errors.name: Paused
errors.msg: Pool is paused: all registry and custody movements are disabled by admin

errors.name: ZeroAmount
errors.msg: Amount must be greater than zero

errors.name: UsdcDecimals
errors.msg: Escrow mint must have exactly 6 decimals (micro-USD seam)

errors.name: WrongSourceOwner
errors.msg: Prepay source account is not owned by the renter's key

errors.name: WrongSourceMint
errors.msg: Prepay source account holds a different mint than this pool custodies

errors.name: WrongDestinationOwner
errors.msg: Refund destination is not owned by the renter

errors.name: WrongDestinationMint
errors.msg: Refund destination holds a different mint than this pool custodies

errors.name: InsufficientClaims
errors.msg: Burn amount exceeds the depositor's claim balance

errors.name: PrepaidInsufficient
errors.msg: Refund amount exceeds the renter's on-chain prepaid record

errors.name: ExitAuthority
errors.msg: Signer is neither the backend authority nor the named identity — one of the two doors is required

errors.name: Overflow
errors.msg: Checked money arithmetic overflowed

errors.name: DeploymentAuthority
errors.msg: Initializer is not this deployment's upgrade authority

errors.name: RootExceedsVault
errors.msg: Root total payout exceeds the vault's USDC — refused, nothing moved

errors.name: InvalidProof
errors.msg: Claim inclusion proof does not verify against the published root

errors.name: WrongPayoutDestination
errors.msg: Payout destination is not owned by the leaf's named depositor

errors.name: RootFrozen
errors.msg: Root payouts are frozen — the root is not Active

errors.name: ChallengeWindowClosed
errors.msg: Challenge window for this root has closed

errors.name: RootNotProvenFalse
errors.msg: Bond slash refused — the root is not proven false

errors.name: SlashExceedsBond
errors.msg: Ruled slash exceeds the bond backing this root

errors.name: ChallengeWindowOpen
errors.msg: Challenge window still open — no payout leaves the vault yet

errors.name: PayoutExceedsTotal
errors.msg: Claim would pay out more than the root's declared total

types.name: AdminAuthorityRotated
docs: Admin authority rotated (multisig migration).

types.name: BackendAuthorityRotated
docs: Backend hot key rotated.

types.name: BondFunded
docs: Bond grew (or was born). `bond_after` mirrors `OperatorBond.amount`.

types.name: BondSlashed
docs: A ruled slash executed — `amount` is EXACTLY the ruled amount.

types.name: ChallengeResolved
docs: The multisig ruled: `root_stands` says which way; `slash_amount` and
`victim` are meaningful only when the root was ruled false.

types.name: ClaimMarker
docs: Proof that leaf `leaf_index` of one root has been paid. Created by `claim`
and never updated: its EXISTENCE is the fact (invariant 3).

fields.name: root
docs: The root this marker belongs to.

fields.name: leaf_index
docs: The leaf that was paid (its index in the window's tree).

fields.name: depositor
docs: The leaf's named depositor — the only identity the payout may reach.

fields.name: amount
docs: Micro-USDC paid out for this leaf.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump of this PDA.

types.name: ClaimPaid
docs: One leaf was paid. A subscriber counts these to rebuild the markers and
the vault.

fields.name: vault_balance_after
docs: Vault USDC AFTER the transfer — the `cash.escrow` mirror.

types.name: ClaimsBurned
docs: A record was exited (burn side of the registry). NO USDC moved.

types.name: ContributionRecorded
docs: A contribution was recorded (mint side of the registry). NO USDC
moved — `amount` is the micro-USD valuation the books attest.

fields.name: supply_after
docs: Claim-mint total supply after the mint — the Σ `claims.contributed`
mirror. Deliberately NOT a vault balance: the vault is untouched.

types.name: OperatorBond
docs: The operator's bond record — the on-chain twin of the bond vault's USDC
balance. One per pool: a bonded operator posts roots against it.

fields.name: amount
docs: Micro-USDC bonded.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump of this PDA.

types.name: PauseToggled
docs: Circuit breaker toggled by admin.

types.name: Pool
docs: The singleton configuration account. Authority model:
* `admin_authority` — the Squads multisig vault PDA (devnet: 2-of-2
founder + teammate). It signs admin instructions only through a
multisig-executed transaction, so every admin action is a 2-of-2 vote.
On-chain this is just a pubkey: whoever can produce its signature
passes, and on devnet only the Squads program can (PDA signature).
* `backend_authority` — the operator's hot key. It signs
deposit/withdraw so members, renters and depositors NEVER need a
wallet (rule 10): the backend submits on their behalf, custodially.

fields.name: admin_authority
docs: Multisig vault PDA — pause/unpause, authority rotations.

fields.name: backend_authority
docs: Operator backend hot key — signs deposit/withdraw (rule 10).

fields.name: usdc_mint
docs: The USDC mint this pool custodies (devnet faucet USDC; SPL Token v3).

fields.name: claim_mint
docs: The claim mint (Token-2022, NonTransferable — the claim registry).

fields.name: vault
docs: Cached vault address for cheap reads/mirroring (derivable from
seeds; stored so external tooling reads ONE account to know everything).

fields.name: paused
docs: Circuit breaker: when true, deposits and withdrawals are refused.
Admin-only toggle — an operator incident response lever, and the
same lever M11's challenge window will use during disputes.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump of the `Pool` PDA itself (needed to sign CPIs as the pool).

fields.name: reserved
docs: Reserved, zero-filled. M11-A (2026-11-26) put settlement STATE in
its own PDA family instead — `settlement.rs`: one root per window,
one marker per leaf, one bond record — because 64 bytes on the
singleton cannot hold a root per window. The challenge-window length
is a published constant
(`settlement::CHALLENGE_WINDOW_SLOTS`), not an argument. This space
stays available for parameters a multisig vote would set; the
account layout itself is unchanged and is not to be redesigned.
Rule-8 guardrail (director-approved 2026-10-31): if the operator fee
band ever goes on-chain, it lands HERE behind a multisig vote — and
a vote alone still never satisfies rule 8: an on-chain band change
additionally requires explicit user approval + a D-log entry.

types.name: PoolOpened
docs: Emitted once, at `initialize`.

types.name: PrepayRecorded
docs: Renter USDC entered escrow — the ONLY inflow (D40). Named for the
action (not `RenterPrepaid`, which is the STATE account's name).

fields.name: vault_balance_after
docs: Vault USDC after the transfer — the `cash.escrow` mirror.

fields.name: prepaid_after
docs: The renter's own prepaid record after the increment.

types.name: PrepayRefunded
docs: Renter USDC left escrow, bounded by their own on-chain record.

types.name: RenterPrepaid
docs: Per-renter prepaid record — the on-chain twin of `prepaid.renter`.
This is the ONLY USDC-denominated record besides the vault itself, and
the two must always reconcile: `vault.amount == Σ prepaid.amount`
(the journey suite asserts it after every renter movement). Renter
money is a LIABILITY (rule 7), so its record is what bounds refunds:
`refund_renter` requires `amount ≤ this.amount` — an on-chain fact,
not an operator attestation.

fields.name: amount
docs: Micro-USDC prepaid and not yet refunded for this renter.

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump of this PDA (stored so refunds never re-derive it).

types.name: RootChallenged
docs: The root froze.

types.name: RootPosted
docs: A root was posted — every immutable field of `SettlementRoot`, plus the
bond snapshot and the slot (the window's origin).

types.name: RootStatus
docs: `RootStatus` is borsh-encoded inside `SettlementRoot` as one byte (the
variant ordinal) — mirrors the way `Pool` stores `paused`.

types.name: Ruling
docs: `Ruling` travels as instruction data (borsh: variant byte, then fields),
so the derive below is what puts it on the wire.

types.name: SettlementRoot
docs: One posted root. Created once per window by `post_root` and never
rewritten: only `status`, `stands_ruled`, `challenger`, `evidence`,
`ruled_slash`, `victim` and `paid_out` ever change after birth — every
other field is write-once (invariant 7 — roots are append-only).

fields.name: pool
docs: The pool this root belongs to (D42: no cross-pool drawing).

fields.name: window
docs: The settlement window — the right half of this account's seeds.

fields.name: merkle_root
docs: The SHA-256 Merkle root over the window's payout leaves.

fields.name: total_payout
docs: Sum of the leaf amounts, as attested by the operator. Checked against
the vault at posting (invariant 1).

fields.name: status
docs: Lifecycle: Active → Challenged → Active | ProvenFalse → Slashed.

fields.name: posted_at
docs: Slot the root was posted in — where the challenge window starts.

fields.name: bond
docs: The operator bond backing THIS root, snapshotted at posting. A later
ruling may not slash more than this (invariant 6).

fields.name: challenger
docs: Who challenged the root (default pubkey while unchallenged).

fields.name: evidence
docs: Commitment to the challenger's off-chain fraud proof — recorded, not
verified: the chain cannot read the books, the multisig reads them.

fields.name: ruled_slash
docs: The exact slash the multisig ruled (0 until a `RootFalse` ruling).

fields.name: victim
docs: Whom the ruled slash pays (default pubkey until ruled).

fields.name: stands_ruled
docs: True once the multisig has ruled the LATEST challenge (if any) to
stand: that ruling waives the rest of the challenge window for this
root (invariant 11). `challenge` clears it.

fields.name: paid_out
docs: Micro-USDC this root has paid out so far. A claim requires
`paid_out + amount <= total_payout` (invariant 12).

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump of this PDA.
